\begin{bankq}[id=SA07-P1-PHY-S3-Q08, source={Score Advanced - Test 07 (16 Apr 2023)}, paper=1, qno=8, type=numerical, subtopic={Vernier and screw gauge}, answer={6.04}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: diameter from a screw gauge with zero error, vernier and screw gauge | steps: pitch 1 mm; zero error +4 divisions; reading}]
In a screw gauge whose least count is 0.005 mm, when no object is present and the screw gauge gap is completely closed the 4$^{\text{th}}$ division on its circular scale coincides with the reference line on main scale reading zero. Now a wire is placed in it to measure its diameter, the reading on the main scale advances by 6 divisions, whereas the circular scale reading becomes 3 times to the corresponding reading when no object was placed. If there are 200 divisions on circular scale, then find the diameter of wire in mm.
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA08-P1-PHY-S3-Q04, source={Score Advanced - Test 08 (22 Apr 2023)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Vernier and screw gauge}, answer={1}, answer_src=key, difficulty=9, diff_parts={K3 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: spring compression from vernier readings, vernier and screw gauge, least count of the vernier | steps: least count of the vernier; compression under the force; proportional change for the shorter spring}]
A vernier calliper has no zero error, one main scale division = 1 mm and 9 main scale division = 10 vernier scale divisions. A spring is held between jaws without exerting force on jaws. Main scale reading is 3.4 cm and 5$^{\text{th}}$ vernier scale division coincides with a main division. When Jaws are pressed by force of 10 N on both sides, main scale reading remains 3.4 cm, but 1$^{\text{st}}$ division of vernier scale coincides with a main scale division. Now spring is removed, cut into two pieces and when one part is inserted between jaws without any force, main scale reading = 1.1 cm and 5$^{\text{th}}$ vernier scale division coincides with a main scale. If we apply force of 30 N on both the jaws, main scale reading remains 1.1 cm and x vernier scale division coincides with a main scale division. Find x.
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=EPS02-P1-PHY-S1-Q02, source={Enthusiast Pre-Score - Test 02 (11 Nov 2020)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=single, subtopic={Experiments}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: unknown resistance and its error from a meter bridge, experiments | steps: balance condition; value; error propagation; least count}]

\begin{bankq}[id=EPS02-P1-PHY-S1-Q04, source={Enthusiast Pre-Score - Test 02 (11 Nov 2020)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=single, subtopic={Errors and measurement}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C2 F0}, diff_note={concepts: Searle method with errors, errors and measurement | steps: least count of screw gauge; diameter; Young modulus; fractional errors}]
The diameter of a wire of length 50 cm is measured with the help of a screw gauge. The main scale reading is 1mm and circular scale reading is 25. Pitch of the screw gauge is 1mm and the total number of divisions on the circular scale is 100. This wire is used in an experiment of determination for the Young's modulus of material of a wire by Searle's method. The wire is placed under a tension of 50 N and elongation of wire is $\ell$ = 0.125 cm. The least count for measuring the length of wire is 0.01 cm and of elongation of the wire is 0.001 cm.\par
(A) The least count in the measurement of diameter of wire is 0.03 mm.\par
(B) The diameter of the wire is $(1.25\pm0.01)$ cm.\par
(C) The percentage error in calculation of Young's modulus is 2.4\%.\par
(D) The Young's modulus of wire is $(5.0\pm0.2)\times10^{10}$ N/m$^2$.
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=EPS02-P1-PHY-S2-Q09, source={Enthusiast Pre-Score - Test 02 (11 Nov 2020)}, paper=1, qno=9, type=multi, subtopic={Errors and measurement}, answer={A,B,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: worm on a free scale with least count, errors and measurement | steps: centre of mass at rest; displacement of the scale; length change; errors}]
A meter scale of mass 0.50 g is placed on smooth horizontal surface. The least count of scale is 0.1 cm. An earthworm of mass 0.25 g is on scale such that length of earthworm is between mark of 4.4 cm and 16.1 cm. The earthworm crawl along the length of meter scale such that its length changes during crawling (but centre of mass remains at geometrical centre of its body). After (10.0 $\pm$ 0.1) sec its length is between mark 20.0 cm and 36.5 cm. Then choose the \textbf{CORRECT} statement (s) :-
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{With respect to ground magnitude of displacement of meter scale is 6.0 cm}
\opt{B}{Change in length of the earthworm is 4.8 cm}
\opt{C}{With respect to meter scale maximum error in measurement of change in length of the earthworm is 0.2 cm}
\opt{D}{With respect to meter scale maximum error in measurement of change in length of the earthworm is 0.4 cm}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{qoptions}

\opt{B}{The least count of scale used to measure length of wire is 1 mm.}

\begin{bankq}[id=EPS02-P2-PHY-S1-Q06, source={Enthusiast Pre-Score - Test 02 (11 Nov 2020)}, paper=2, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={Errors and measurement}, answer={B,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: reported length with error, errors and measurement | steps: mean; error; significant figures}]

12.66 mm, 12.58 mm, 12.62 mm, 12.80 mm and 12.72 mm\par
The experimenter reported the result of the experiment based on the above readings.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Number of significant figures in the length reported will be 3.}

\begin{bankq}[id=EPS02-P2-PHY-S3-Q05, source={Enthusiast Pre-Score - Test 02 (11 Nov 2020)}, paper=2, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Errors and measurement}, answer={4.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: refractive index with fit error, errors and measurement | steps: slope of the fit; refractive index; error}]
Snell's law relation for air glass boundary is given by equation $n_{air}\sin\theta_i=n_{glass}\sin\theta_r$. Here angle of refraction in glass is $\theta_r$ and the angle of incident in air is $\theta_i$. The refractive index of air is n$_{air}$= 1 (with negligible uncertainty). In an experiment to verify Snell's Law, the best fit line on a graph between sin$\theta_r$ (on the y-axis) and sin$\theta_i$ (on the x-axis) is given by the equation $y=(6.66\pm0.05)\times10^{-1}x+(0.022\pm0.024)$. The refractive index of the glass, including the error is reported as 1.ab $\pm$ 0.0c, where a, b and c are digits after the decimal point. Calculate value of $(a+b-c)$.
\end{bankq}
